3824 SHRI SUBHASISH KHUNTIA: 
 
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the current status of tourism infrastructure development projects in Odisha, including airports, 
roads, and hotels; 
(b)  the funds allocated for infrastructure improvement in tourist destinations in Odisha over the 
last five years; 
(c)  the challenges faced in developing infrastructure in remote tourist locations in the State; and 
(d)  the Ministry’s plans to collaborate with the Odisha Government to improve tourism 
infrastructure? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM                                      (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (d):  Development and promotion of tourist destinations and products is undertaken by the 
respective State Government/Union Territory (UT) Administration. The Ministry of Tourism through 
its central sector schemes of ‘Swadesh Darshan (SD)’ and ‘Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual, 
Heritage Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD)’ complements the efforts of tourism infrastructure 
development in the country by extending financial assistance to the State Governments/UT 
Administrations including the State of Odisha.  
 
The scheme guidelines inter -alia provides for development of Tourist Facilitation Centre, tourist 
Information Centre, log huts, Amphitheatre, Foot -over Bridges, Signages, CCTVs, last mile road 
connectivity, façade illumination, basic amenities such as Toilets, dustbins, drinking water facilities, 
drainage & waste management facilities and other site development works such as benches, 
landscaping, flooring, railings etc. at tourist destinations.  
 
Further, Ministry of Tourism works closely with Ministry of Road Transport and Ministry of Civil 
Aviation for improving road and air connectivity to tourist destinations. Under RCS UDAN, Ministry 
of Tourism collaborated with Ministry of Civil Aviation and shared the Viability Gap Funding (VGF) 
amount for 53 tourism routes identified. 
 
The Government of India under the guidelines for Special Assistance to States/Union Territories for 
Capital Investment (SASCI) for Development of Iconic Tourist Centres has approved two projects in 
Odisha. 
 
Details of funds sanctioned for the State of Odisha under the aforesaid schemes of Ministry of 
Tourism is annexed. 
 
Ministry of Tourism work in close coordination with State Governments/UT Administrations, local 
authorities, and stakeholders to overcome the challenges and unlock the full potential of remote tourist 
destinations, making them accessible and attractive to travelers while fostering local economic growth. 
 
Proposals from States and Union Territories seeking financial assistance under various schemes of the 
Ministry of Tourism are received from time to time. Funding for these projects is granted based on 
compliance with the stipulated provisions and the availability of funds.

Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the various challenges faced by the tourism industry in Uttar Pradesh (UP) that are 
hampering the full potential of the State's rich heritage and cultural attractions, the details of 
the challenges on the basis of the factors responsible; 
(b) the various schemes and policies of Government through which measures are being taken to 
improve these areas and the details of achievements in the last five years, particularly in 
relation to major attractions; and 
(c) the amount allocated and spent in UP for this purpose in the l ast five years, year -wise and

efforts of States/UTs by developing and promoting various tourism products of the country, 
including in Uttar Pradesh through various schemes and initiatives. To enhance the experience of 
the tourists, Ministry of Tourism has taken the following initiatives:- 
• To enhance tourism infrastructure in the country, the Ministry of Tourism through its central 
sector schemes of ‘Swadesh Darshan (SD)’, ‘Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual, 
Heritage Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD)’ and ‘Assistance to Central Agencies for 
Tourism Infrastructure Development’ extends financial assistance to the State 
Governments/UT Administrations/Central Agencies including the State of Uttar Pradesh.

Darshan 2.0 (SD 2.0) with the objective to develop sustainable and responsible tourism

Investment (SASCI Scheme) - Development of Iconic Tourist Centers to Global Scale has 
sanctioned two projects in Uttar Pradesh.

Governments/Union Territory (UT) Administrations for setting up of dedicated Tourism 
Police. The State Governments of Uttar Pradesh have deployed tourist police, in one form 
or the other.

initiated Travel for LiFE programme to promote sustainable tourism in the country and to 
encourage the tourists and tourism businesses to adopt sustainable tourism practices.

(CBSP) Scheme to train and upgrade manpower to provide better service standards.

Tourist Facilitator (IITF) Certification Programme – a Pan-India online learning program.

engagement through website etc. In addition, Indian Missions overseas also undertake 
various promotional activities to attract more global travelers to various tourist destinations 
of the country.

STADIUM IN TRIBAL AREAS OF JHARKHAND 
 
3833 #.    SHRI PRADIP KUMAR VARMA: 
 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state :- 
  
(a) whether due to absence of adequate sports stadiums and lack of facilities in the tribal dominated 
areas of Jharkhand the players get inadequate opportunity for daily practice due to which the 
development of sports talent is hindered; 
 
(b) whether there has been a persistent demand from public representatives over the years for 
setting up open stadiums in the headquarters of tribal-dominated districts across Jharkhand; and 
 
(c) if so, the details of the demands and the steps taken in this regard? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS  
 
(DR. MANSUKH MANDAVIYA) 
 
(a) to (c) ‘Sports’ being a State subject, the responsibility of development of sports, including setting up 
open stadiums in the country , rests primarily with the respective State/Union Territory Governments. The 
Union Government only supplements their efforts by bridging critical gaps. However, the Khelo India 
Scheme and National Sports Development Fund (NSDF), implemented by this Ministry, under 
which financial assistance for development of sports infrastructure, including sports stadia, is 
provided, are demand-driven schemes. The proposals received from the State/UT Governments and 
other eligible entities are considered for financial support, subject to their completeness, technical 
feasibility and availability of funds under the Scheme . No such proposal to set up open stadiums in 
the headquarters of tribal -dominated districts across Jharkhand  is pending in the Ministry. The 
details of the sports infrastructure projects approved and their sanctioned cost, funds released and 
their physical and financial progress, under Khelo India Scheme and NSDF, across the country, 
including in the State of Jharkhand, are available in public domain on the dashboards of the 
Ministry at https://mdsd.kheloindia.gov.in and http://www.nsdf.yas.gov.in/nsdf -glance.html. 
Further, the details of Khelo India Centres (KICs) notified and sports academies accredited under 
the Khelo India Scheme, across the country, including  in the State of Jharkhand, are available in 
public domain on the dashboard of the Ministry at https://dashboard.kheloindia.gov.in/state -wise-
khelo-india-centers.

(a) the key objectives and goals of the Khelo India scheme, and how it has evolved over the years; 
 
(b) the amount of funds allocated for the implementation of the Khelo India scheme from  2021-
2024, and the major areas of focus for the upcoming years; 
 
(c) the number of new sports infrastructure projects that have been approved under the  scheme and

(DR. MANSUKH MANDAVIYA)

across the country , focusing on grassroots development and talent nurturing. Initially centred on

into 5 components viz. creation and upgrading of sports infrastructure, sports competitions and 
talent development, Khelo India Centres and sports academies, the Fit India Movement, and the 
promotion of inclusiveness through sports. Key achievements under the Scheme include approval of 
321 new sports infrastructure projects, notification of 1045 Khelo India Centres (KICs) , 34 Khelo 
India State Centres of Excellence (KISCEs), accreditation of 306 sports academies aimed at training 
children, supporting former athletes, and enhancing grassroots sports infrastructure.  So far, 1 7 
editions of the Khelo India Games have been conducted, with participation from over 50,000 
athletes. The scheme has identified and supported 2 845 Khelo India Athletes (KIAs)  across the 
country who are provided with  coaching, equipment, medical care, and a monthly Out of Pocket

क्या विवि और न्याय मंत्री यह बताने की क ृ पा करेंगे वक :

(ख) वपछले तीन िर्षों में एलएडीसीएस क े  माध्यम से विचाररत और सुलझाए गए मामलों की क ु ल संख्या 
का राज्य-िार और आंध्र प्रिेश क े  वलए विला-िार ब्यौरा क्या है ; 
(ग) एलएडीसीएस क े  तहत शावमल वकए गए स्टाफ/बचाि (वडफ ें स) परामशयिाताओं की क ु ल संख्या का 
राज्य-िार और आंध्र प्रिेश क े  वलए विला-िार ब्यौरा क्या है ; और  
(घ) वपछले तीन िर्षों क े  िौरान एलएडीसीएस क े  तहत संवितररत की गई वनवि का राज्य-िार और आंध्र

ऩयभाणु ऊजाा विबाग (डीएई) के  तहत एक  सािाजननक  ऺेत्र के  उद्मभ मूयेनन मभ कॉयऩोयेशन

फनाए  यखने  के  र्रए, सभम-सभम ऩय, ऐसी ऩरयमोजनाओां की मोजना  फनाई  जाती  है जजसभें 
क ुछ भौज ूद ा इकाइमों के  ऺभता विस्ताय के  साथ -साथ  देश  के  विर्बन्न दहस्सों भें नई 
ऩरयमोजनाओां की  स्थाऩना  शार्भर है।  
 
नार्बकीम ईंधन सजमभश्र (एनएपसी) ने हैदयाफाद भें जस्थत अऩनी प्रायांर्बक स्थाऩना भें ईंधन

प्लेर्फॉम ट एग्रीग ेर्र म ॉड्यूल के म ाध्यम  से, प्लेर्फॉमट एग्रीगेर्र प्लेर्फॉमट कामगारों  के र्ेर्ा को ई -श्रम पोर्टल 
पर सत्यावपत/अपलोर् क र सक ते हैं और इसके अलाव ा एग्रीग ेर्सट न े अपन े साथ जुडे प्लेर्फॉमट कामगारों  को ई -श्रम

(क) से (घ) : िेश भर में त्वररत न्याय प्रिान करने क े  वलए अिीनस्थ न्यायालयों की स्थापना, विसक े  
अंतगयत त्वररत वनपटान न्यायालय (एफटीसी) भी हैं, राज्य/संघ राज्यक्षेत्र सरकारों क े  काययक्षेत्र में आते हैं, 
िो उनक े  संबद्ध उच्च न्यायालयों क े  परामशय से अपनी आिश्यकता और संसािनों क े  अनुसार ऐसे 
न्यायालयों की स्थापना करते हैं। भारत सरकार द्वारा स्थावपत वकए गए 14िें वित्त आयोग ने 2015-2020 
क े  िौरान िघन्य प्रक ृ वत क े  विवनवियष्ट मामलों, मवहलाओं, बालकों, िररष्ठ नागररकों, विव्ांगिनों, मरणांत 
रोगों से संक्रवमत व्क्तियों, आवि से संबंवित वसविल मामले तथा संपवत्तयों से संबंवित मामले, िो पांच

को दिर्ा जाने वाला उत्तर 
 
ओडिशा में पययटन अवसंरचना का ववकास  
 
3824 श्री शुभाशीष खुंटट या: 
क्र्ा पययटन मंत्री र्ह बत ाने क ी क ृपा क रेंगे कक : 
(क ) ओडिशा में ववमानपत्तनों, सड़कों और होटलों सदहत पर्यटन अवसंरचना ववकास पररर्ोजनाओं 
की वतयमान स्थितत क्र्ा है; 
(ि) वव गत  पांच व र्षों के िौरान ओडिशा में पर्यटन थिल ों में अव संरचना सुध ार के लल ए कक त नी 
धनरालश आवंदटत की गई है ; 
(ग) राज्र् में िूरिराज के पर्यटन थिलों में अवसंरचना ववकलसत  करने में  क्र्ा चुनौततर्ां आई हैं; 
और 
(घ) पर्यटन अव संरचना में सुध ार के लल ए ओडिशा सरक ार के साि सहर्ोग क रने क ी मंत्राल र् क ी 
क्र्ा र्ोजनाएं हैं? 
 
उत्तर 
पययटन मंत्री      (श्री गजेन्द्र ससंह शेखावत) 
 
(क) से (घ) : पर्यटन थिलों और उत्पािों का ववकास और संवधयन संबंधधत राज्र् सरकार /संघ 
राज्र्क्षेत्र प्रशासन द्वारा ककर्ा जाता है। पर्यटन मंत्रालर् ‘थविेश िशयन (एसिी) ’ और ‘तीियथिल 
जीर्णोद्धार एवं  आध्र्ास्त्मक, ववरासत संवधयन अलभर्ान (प्रशाि) ’ नामक अपनी क ें द्रीर् क्षेत्र की 
र्ोजनाओं के माध्र्म से ओडिशा राज्र् सदहत राज्र् सरकारों/संघ राज्र्क्षेत्र प्रशासनों को ववत्तीर् 
सहार्त ा प्रिान क रके िेश में पर्यटन अव संरचना के वव क ास के प्रर्ासों क ो संपूररत करता  है। 
 
र्ोजना के दिशा-तनिेशों में पर्यटन थिलों पर अन्र् बातों के साि-साि पर्यटक  सुवव ध ा कें द्र, पर्यटक 
सूचना कें द्र, लॉग हट्स, एम्फीधिएटर, फुट-ओवर ब्रिज, साइनेज, सीसीटीवी , अंततम छोर तक सड़क 
संपकय , अग्रभाग की प्रकाश व्र्वथिा, मूल भूत  सुवव ध ाएं जैसे शौचाल र्, कूड़ेिान, पेर्जल  सुवव ध ाएं,

Friday, the 4th  April, 2025/14 Chaitra, 1947 (Saka) 
The House met at eleven of the clock, 
MR. CHAIRMAN in the Chair. 
BIRTHDAY GREETINGS 
MR. CHAIRMAN:   Hon. Members, the entire House must rejoice and share the joy of 
those whose birthday is today or tomorrow.  Pleased to extend birthday greetings to 
hon. Members of Parliament, Shri Shaktisinh Gohil, Shri Arun Singh , -- what a 
coincidence   the   two   veterans   having  their  birthdays  on  the same   date  -- 
Shri  Sukhendu Sekhar Ray and Shri R. Dharmar.  Their birthdays are tomorrow - 
April 5.  …(Interruptions)…   
SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH (karnataka):  Si r, what about those Members, whose 
birthday fall next week? 
MR. CHAIRMAN :  Hon. Members, when the House is not in Session, I have the 
extreme pleasure and satisfaction to directly talk to those hon. Members and greet 
them.    
Shri Shaktisinh Gohil  represents -- can I say, ‘the glorious State of Gujarat’ -- 
in this august House since June, 2020.  Prior to this, Shri Shaktisinh Gohil has served 
four terms as a Member of the Gujarat Legislative Assembly, from 1990-95, a period I 
share with you, -- you were in the Assemb ly, I was in the Parliament -- then, from 
1995-98, 2007-2012, and 2014-201 7. He held key positions, including Minister of 
State for Finance, Education, and Health in the Government of Gujarat, and he also 
hailed the position of the Leader of Opposi tion in the Gujarat Legislative Assembly 
when the Leader of the House, the then Ch ief Minister, now the Prime Minister of the 
country, was in his third term.  Shri Shaktisinh Gohil   has represented India at various 
international conferences.  More is coming.  …(Interruptions)…  
SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH:  Sir, marital status क्या है? 
MR. CHAIRMAN:  Well, he shares it with very distin guished people.  Shri Shaktisinh 
Gohil has represented India at various in ternational conferences valuably 

strengthening democratic dialogue and par liamentary governance worldwide.  He is 
an extremely involved Member of this House, making sharp incisive and well thought 
out contributions.  He happens to be a di stinguished advocate and agriculturist.  He 
has keen interest in regional languages and fo lk music.  An avid sports enthusiast, he 
has led local cricket clubs an d has been actively engaged in cricket, volleyball, and 
chess.  On your birthday, my suggestion is, take parliamentary work also sportingly.   
Shri Arun Singh  is representing the State of Uttar Pradesh in this august 
House, for a second term (2019-2020 an d 2020-present).  A Chartered Accountant 
by profession, Shri Singh believes in auditi ng himself before auditing others in his 
organizational duties.  He has made significan t contributions in public life, in the field 
of finance and management.  His tenure as Director of the State Bank of India and the 
Union Bank for seven years is remembered for the pivotal ro le he played in bringing 
about transparency and accountability.  
Shri Arun Singh had worked on key pr ojects with the World Bank and the 
United Nations. Shri Singh plays a critical role in his organization as the National 
General Secretary of BJP. Shri Singh also has the distinction of being Secretary of the 
Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Research Foundation. 
Married to Shrimati Meenakshi Singh, the couple is blessed with 
daughters, Ikshita Singh and Ashmita Singh and son Akshit Singh. 
Shri Sukhendu Sekhar Ray  – a picture of politeness and grace – who always 
believes in rule-based regime, is also an  advocate like me and currently serving his 
third term in this august House,  continually from 2011, namely , first time from 2011 to 
2017, then from 2017 to 2023 and from 2023  still counting.  He is a veteran leader of 
the All India Trinamool Congress, consistent ly working at the grassroots with sublime 
commitment to public service. He has al ways been participant in parliamentary 
debates, exhibiting due diligence and highest consideration to the Chair. 
His nomination to the Panel of Vice -Chairpersons for seven times (July 
2014,  April 2018,   July 2020,  July 2022,  December 2022,  July  2023  and June 2024) 
reflects his keen interest in parliament ary decorum and knowledge of procedure. 
Beyond his legislative role, Shri Ray was Member of the National Jute Board (2015-
2020) and that incidentally takes care of  about four million farmers.  The hon. 
Agriculture Minister is here.  He served as  the Vice-President of the Calcutta High 
Court Bar Association from 2009 to 2011.  A prolific writer, Sh ri Ray has authored 
several notable books, including Chayatarini (2009) and Pranab Mukherjee – The 
All-Season Man (2010) and has also served as the editor of Jago Bangla, a Bengali 
daily.

Married to the late Shrimati Mahashweta Ray, the couple is blessed with 
daughter, Saswati Ray. 
Shri R. Dharmar  is representing the State of Tamil Nadu in this august House 
as a Member of Parliament since June 2022, serving his first term. 
An agriculturist by profession, Shri Dharmar holds a B.A. degree and, as a 
dedicated member of the AIADMK party, continues to serve the people of Tamil Nadu 
in all earnestness and commitment.  Widely  respected as a local leader, he has 
earned a strong reputation as a grassroots representative tirelessly addressing the 
needs and aspirations of his communi ty and others. He was married to  late Shrimati 
Sivakami; the couple is blesses with daughters — Anandi and Indupriya. 
Hon. Members, on my own and on behalf of this House, I wish them a long, 
healthy and happy life and extend greetings to their family members and friends.  
FAREWELL TO THE RETIRING MEMBERS 
MR. CHAIRMAN : Hon. Members, ...(Interruptions)...  One minute, equally 
important is Farewell.  Hon. Members, reception of Members in this House and 
farewell are very touching moments.  Fare well is not a disconnect. It is only their 
absence from the House and sometimes, for the Members of this House, more often 
than not, their presence is as impactful as their absen ce.  Two of our esteemed 
colleagues, Shri Birendra Prasad Baishya an d Shri Mission Ranjan Das, representing 
the State of Assam, will retire from this Hous e in their present term on June 14, 2025. 
All of us will miss their presence as thei r dedicated service and contributions have 
enriched the deliberations and their informed discourse has been enlightening.  
Shri Birendra Prasad Baishya , a senior parliamentarian and an experienced 
leader, has served as a Member of the Elev enth Lok Sabha and, now, in his second 
term in the Rajya Sabha. He has also held the office of the Union Minister of Steel and 
Mines, from 1996 to 1998.  Shri Baishya has been a distinguished voice in this House, 
actively engaging in discussions on key i ssues concerning Assam’s development and 
the welfare of its people. He has been ever alert to seek attention of the Chair.  His 
keen insights and unwavering commitmen t to societal upliftment are truly 
commendable. Notably, his dedication to pu blic causes, particularly in promoting 
sports and youth development, has been remarkable. His contributions to policy 
discussions, especially in infrastructure, in dustrial growth and social justice, will be

appreciated the phenomenal development in the North-East.  
Shri Mission Ranjan Das , a dedicated public servant and a staunch advocate 
for the rights of the people of Assam, br ings with him vast legislative experience, 
having served four terms as a Member of  the Assam Legislativ e Assembly. He has 
also held key positions as Chairman of the Assam Industrial Development Corporation 
and the Assam State Transport Corporation, contributing significantly to the State’s 
economic and infrastructural growth.  His act ive participation in legislative debates

On behalf of the entire House, I extend my best wishes to Shri Birendra Prasad
